questions.stem: The horizontal double-headed arrow at the top of this tracing spans from one R wave to the next. Measuring this distance is used to determine what?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The amplitude of the P wave

explanation.summary: The R-R interval is the time between successive R waves; because it represents one full beat-to-beat cycle, it is used to calculate heart rate.
explanation.whyCorrect: The R-R interval is the time between successive R waves; because it represents one full beat-to-beat cycle, it is used to calculate heart rate.

questions.stem: This tracing shows sequential values (300, 150, 100, 75, 60, 50) assigned to heavy gridlines after a starting R wave. What is this technique used to estimate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The heart rate based on where the next R wave falls

explanation.summary: The 300-150-100-75-60-50 rule estimates rate: starting on an R wave, each successive heavy gridline where the next R wave lands corresponds to that rate in beats per minute.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 300-150-100-75-60-50 rule estimates rate: starting on an R wave, each successive heavy gridline where the next R wave lands corresponds to that rate in beats per minute.

questions.stem: What type of diagnostic recording is shown here?

explanation.summary: The simultaneous display of the six limb leads (I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF) and six precordial leads (V1-V6) on pink graph paper is the standard format of a 12-lead ECG, which records the heart's electrical activity from multiple spatial vantage points.
explanation.whyCorrect: The simultaneous display of the six limb leads (I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF) and six precordial leads (V1-V6) on pink graph paper is the standard format of a 12-lead ECG, which records the heart's electrical activity from multiple spatial vantage points.

questions.stem: This torso diagram with arrows radiating from the heart best illustrates which concept underlying ECG interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The distribution of autonomic nerves to the heart

choices.label: B
choices.text: The coronary artery blood supply to each myocardial region

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sequence of valve closures during the cardiac cycle

choices.label: D
choices.text: The anatomical location of the cardiac conduction pathways

choices.label: E
choices.text: Each ECG lead views cardiac electrical activity from a different directional vector

explanation.summary: The arrows show that the limb leads (frontal plane) and precordial leads (horizontal plane) each 'look at' the heart's depolarization from a distinct angle. Combining these views lets the ECG localize electrical events in three dimensions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The arrows show that the limb leads (frontal plane) and precordial leads (horizontal plane) each 'look at' the heart's depolarization from a distinct angle. Combining these views lets the ECG localize electrical events in three dimensions.

questions.stem: The precordial (chest) leads V1-V6 record cardiac activity primarily in which of the two planes highlighted here?

explanation.summary: The chest (precordial) leads V1-V6 encircle the heart in a transverse cut and therefore assess electrical vectors in the horizontal plane, whereas the limb leads assess the frontal plane.
explanation.whyCorrect: The chest (precordial) leads V1-V6 encircle the heart in a transverse cut and therefore assess electrical vectors in the horizontal plane, whereas the limb leads assess the frontal plane.

questions.stem: This rhythm strip shows a wide, polymorphic complex whose amplitude progressively waxes and wanes around the baseline. What is the rhythm?

explanation.summary: The continuously changing QRS amplitude that appears to 'twist' around the isoelectric baseline is characteristic of torsades de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a prolonged QT interval.
explanation.whyCorrect: The continuously changing QRS amplitude that appears to 'twist' around the isoelectric baseline is characteristic of torsades de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a prolonged QT interval.

questions.topicName: Electrocardiogram: Waves, Intervals, and Segments (2 of 2)
questions.stem: On this labeled tracing, the PR interval, ST segment, and QT interval are marked. What does the PR interval primarily measure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The time the ventricles remain in systole

choices.label: C
choices.text: The time of ventricular repolarization only

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total duration of the cardiac cycle

choices.label: E
choices.text: The time for the impulse to travel from atrial depolarization through the AV node to the ventricles

explanation.summary: The PR interval spans the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS, reflecting conduction from atrial depolarization through the AV node (including the physiologic AV delay) to the ventricles.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PR interval spans the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS, reflecting conduction from atrial depolarization through the AV node (including the physiologic AV delay) to the ventricles.

questions.topicName: Electrocardiogram: Waves, Intervals, and Segments (2 of 2)
questions.stem: This figure maps the ECG waves onto atrial and ventricular systole and diastole across one cardiac cycle. Ventricular systole begins immediately after which electrical event?

choices.label: D
choices.text: SA node firing during atrial diastole

explanation.summary: Ventricular contraction (systole) follows ventricular depolarization; the QRS triggers the mechanical contraction, while ventricular relaxation (diastole) follows the T wave (repolarization).
explanation.whyCorrect: Ventricular contraction (systole) follows ventricular depolarization; the QRS triggers the mechanical contraction, while ventricular relaxation (diastole) follows the T wave (repolarization).

questions.topicName: Electrocardiogram: Waves, Intervals, and Segments (2 of 2)
questions.stem: During the ST segment marked on this ECG tracing, what is the electrical state of the ventricular myocardium?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Partially repolarizing from apex to base

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uniformly depolarized (plateau phase, no net current flow)

explanation.summary: The ST segment is isoelectric because the entire ventricular myocardium is depolarized at the same time (plateau phase). With no potential difference across the heart, no net current is recorded, so the trace returns to baseline between the QRS and T wave.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ST segment is isoelectric because the entire ventricular myocardium is depolarized at the same time (plateau phase). With no potential difference across the heart, no net current is recorded, so the trace returns to baseline between the QRS and T wave.
